As indicated earlier in this Provisional Findings, the TCCC is alleged to have

I../

in the relevant market fits a theory of harm of priq\e\disfcrimination.

Price discrimination is a term that econorfusts\''use to describe the practice of
•r--
selling the same product to different cus_t6mers at different prices even though
the cost of sale is the same. More,pre9i§`ely, it is se[[ing at a price or prices such
that the ratio of price to margi<n?i\6o\sts is different in different sales3.
Other literature defines pri'`?e,`discrimination in markets for tangible products and
(, y/y``,
services as selling th6'' sa"me product to different customers for different prices
when those differ6n\`6es are not justified by differences in costs.
Several case` laws have established that, price discrimination may be
exploitative of customers, for example, where higher prices are charged to
"locked in" customers unable to switch to alternative suppliers; it can also be
ha-rmful to the competitive process, where it leads to a distortion of competition
in the markets downstream of the dominant undertaking. The case law
establishes that, in determining whether there is discrimination in the form of the
application of dissimilar conditions to equivalent transactions with other trading
parties, thereby placing the discriminated party at a competitive disadvantage,
five issues must be addressed:

Upon analysis, it was concluded that pre- and post-merger scenarios will remain the same for both perspectives of Section 5 (6) (a) and (b) of the Fair Competition Act, 2003, and thus having no possibility of either creating or strengthening a position of dominance in the relevant market. text:
HOTUBA YA MHE. DKT. ASHATU K. KIJAJI (MB), WAZIRI WA VIWANDA
NA BIASHARA WAKATI WA MKUTANO WA KILELE CHA SIKU YA
USHINDANI DUNIANI KATIKA UKUMBI WA MIKUTANO WA SERENGETI,
JENGO LA USHINDANI (USHINDANI HOUSE), JIJINI DAR ES SALAAM
TAREHE 5 DISEMBA, 2023
Mwenyekiti wa Tume ya Ushindani (FCC) Dkt. Aggrey Mlimuka,
Wajumbe wa Tume (FCC),
Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa FCC Bw. William Erio,
Mkurugenzi Mkuu Shirika la Viwango Tanzania, Dr. Athuman Y. Ngenya,
Mkurugenzi Mtendaji Kituo cha Uwekezaji Tanzania, Ndg. Gilead J. Teri,
Afisa Mtendaji Mkuu Wakala wa Usajili wa Biashara na Leseni (BRELA), Ndg.
Godfrey Nyaisa,
Wawakilishi wa Mamlaka ya Ushindani ya Jumuiya ya Afrika Mashariki,
Wawakilishi wa Trade Marks East Africa (TMEA),
Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa Shirika la Mawasiliano Tanzania,
Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa Shirika la Kuhudumia Viwanda Vidogo (SIDO),
Mtendaji Mkuu wa Wakala wa Vipimo (WMA),
Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa Shirikia la Maendeleo la Taifa (NDC),
Mkurugenzi Mtendaji wa Kituo cha Uwekezaji Tanzania (TIC),
Menejimenti na Watumishi wa Tume ya Ushindani,
Wawakilishi kutoka Wizara, Idara na Taasisi za Serikali,
Wawakilishi wa jumuiya za wachimbaji wadogo wa madini kutoka Kanda ya Ziwa,
Wawakilishi wa wazalishaji na wasambazaji wa mbegu kutoka Kanda ya Kaskazini,
Wawakilishi wa wakamuaji wa mchuzi wa zabibu na mafuta ya alizeti kutoka Kanda
ya Kati,
1

Wawakilishi wa wenye viwanda na wafanyabiashara kutoka Kanda ya Nyanda za
Juu Kusini,
Wawakilishi wa wakulima wa korosho kutoka Kanda ya Mashariki,
Wageni waalikwa,
Wanahabari,
Mabibi na Mabwana,
Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania!
Napenda nianze kwanza kwa kumshukuru sana Mwenyezi Mungu, mwingi wa
rehema na fadhili kwa kutujalia afya njema na kutuwezesha kujumuika pamoja kwa
ajili ya kushiriki shughuli hii muhimu ya kuadhimisha Kilele cha Siku ya Ushindani
Duniani inayofanyika kitaifa hapa Dar es Salaam.
Pili, nitumie fursa hii kuishukuru FCC kwa kunialika katika maadhimisho haya. Pia,
napenda kuwapongeza kwa maandalizi na uratibu mzuri wa maadhimisho haya ya
Siku ya Ushindani Duniani, hongereni sana!
Aidha, nitumie fursa hii pia kuwashukuru kwa dhati wadau na waalikwa wote kwa
kuitikia wito wa kuhudhuria shughuli hii muhimu ya kilele cha maadhimisho ya Siku
ya Ushindani Duniani kwa mwaka 2023, licha ya majukumu mengine mliyonayo,
tunawashukuru sana!
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, sisi sote tunafahamu kuwa lengo la
kufanya biashara yoyote ile ni kupata faida. Katika kufikia lengo hilo mbinu
mbalimbali hutumiwa na wafanyabiashara zikiwemo mbinu halali zinazosaidia
kuongeza ubunifu na kukuza biashara baina ya washindani na zile zisizo halali na
zisizo stahili yaani zile zinazokiuka sheria, kanuni na taratibu zilizopo ambazo ni
changamoto kubwa inayosababisha athari hasi katika ustawi wa biashara na
uchumi kwa ujumla.
Kutokana na changamoto hii, Baraza la Umoja wa Mataifa kupitia Uamuzi Namba
34/447 wa Disemba 19, 1979, katika kikao chake cha Aprili 8 hadi 22, 1980,
kilipitisha kanuni na Taratibu za Kudhibiti Vitendo Vinavyofifisha Biashara Duniani
(The Set of Multilaterally Agreed Equitable Principles and Rules for the
Control of Restrictive Business Practices). Kuanzia kipindi hicho, Kanuni hizi
2

zimekuwa chachu ya kuundwa kwa Sheria za Ushindani ulimwenguni kote chini ya
uratibu wa Shirika la Umoja wa Mataifa la Biashara na Maendeleo (UNCTAD).
Huu ndio ulikuwa msingi wa kuanzisha Maadhimisho ya Siku ya Ushindani Duniani
ili kukumbuka kuasisiwa kwa juhudi za kudhibiti vitendo vinavyofifisha ushindani
katika biashara ulimwenguni, kila ifikapo tarehe 5 Disemba.
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, vitendo vinavyofifisha ushindani, ambavyo
ndio msingi wa sheria ya ushindani duniani kote vimegawanyika katika makundi
yafuatayo:
1. Makubaliano yanayofifisha Ushindani (Anti-Competitive Agreements).
Vitendo hivi ni pamoja na:
a. Washindani kukutana na kupanga bei za bidhaa na huduma;
b. Washindani kukubaliana kiasi cha bidhaa kinachozalishwa (output
restriction);
c. Washindani kugoma kupeleka bidhaa sokoni (collective boycott);
d. Washindani kukubaliana namna ya kuomba zabuni pale zabuni
zinapotangazwa (bid rigging);
2. Matumizi mabaya ya nguvu ya soko (abuse/misuse of market power) kwa
kampuni zenye hodhi kubwa ya soko.
3. Miungano ya kampuni yenye lengo la kuimarisha hodhi ya soko kufanyika na
kuathiri ushindani na walaji katika soko.
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, kila mwaka katika kuadhimisha
maadhimisho haya huwa kunakuwa na kaulimbiu inayotuongoza. Kauli mbiu ya
mwaka 2023 ni “Prioritizing Socially Sensitive Sectors” ambayo kwa upande wa
Tanzania imetoholewa kuwa “Cartel and their harmful effect on consumers” yaani
“Njama baina ya washindani na madhara yake kwa walaji na watumiaji”.
Kaulimbiu hii imekuja wakati muafaka kwani dunia bado inaendelea kukabiliana na
madhara ya majanga makubwa mawili ya Uviko wa 19 “COVID-19” na vita ya
Ukraine na Rushia ambavyo vimesababisha kupanda kwa bei za bidhaa na
huduma. Hali hii inatoa tashwishi kwa wafanyabiashara kutafuta njia ya kuongeza
faida katika biashara zao kwa kila njama ‘cartels’.Jambo hili litaleta athari hasi kwa
uchumi na maendeleo ya Taifa na kukwamisha juhudi za Serikali ya awamu ya sita
3

za kuleta maendeleo endelevu kwa wananchi. Nitumie fursa hii kama Serikali
kuwataka wafanyabiashara kujiepusha na ‘cartels’ na FCC kama mamlaka ya
udhibiti “Regulator” kufuatilia kwa karibu hali ya soko.
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, nimetaarifiwa kuwa katika kuadhimisha
siku hii, FCC ilifanya semina kwa wadau mbalimbali katika Kanda inayozisimamia
kama ifuatavyo;
(i) Wachimbaji wadogo wa madini katika Kanda ya Ziwa;
(ii) Wazalishaji na wasambazaji wa mbegu kutoka Kanda ya Kaskazini,
Arusha
(iii) Wakamuaji wa mchuzi wa zabibu na mafuta ya alizeti kutoka Makao
Makuu ya FCC - Dodoma,
(iv) Wenye viwanda na wafanyabiashara kutoka Kanda ya Nyanda za Juu
Kusini - Mbeya,
(v) Wakulima wa korosho kutoka Kanda ya Mashariki – Mtwara.
Aidha, nimefahamishwa pia wawakilishi wa wadau kutoka kila Kanda tajwa wapo
hapa ambapo kimsingi wanaitumia fursa ya maadhimisho haya kwa ajili ya
kujifunza na kujionea wenyewe jinsi changamoto wanazokutana nazo katika
maeneo yao zitakavyoshughulikiwa na FCC kwa mujibu wa taratibu zilizopo na kwa
mujibu wa misingi ya ushindani.
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, Sheria ya Ushindani ina umuhimu mkubwa
sana katika kujenga uchumi. Hivyo Tukifanya biashara zetu kwa kufuata misingi ya
ushindani tutapata faida zifuatazo;;
(i) Kuongeza ufanisi katika uzalishaji na usambazaji wa bidhaa na huduma;
(ii) Kukuza ubunifu; ikiwa ni pamoja na
(iii) Kuboresha matumizi ya rasilimali kwa kuzingatia ufanisi.
Faida hizi zitatufanya tuweze kushindana katika masoko ya kikanda na kimataifa
ikizingatiwa kuwa Tanzania tayari tupo kwenye Soko huru la Biashara Africa yaani
AfCFTA. Hivyo, bila kufuata misingi hii Tanzania inaweza kuwa soko la bidhaa za
wenzetu.
4

Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, naamini tumesikia maelezo mazuri
yaliyobainishwa na Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa FCC kuhusu majukumu ya msingi
yanayotekelezwa na FCC katika kudhibiti na kusimamia soko la Tanzania bara
kuhakikisha kuwa washiriki wake hususan wafanyabiashara / kampuni
zinazoshindana kibiashara, zinazingatia misingi ya ushindani sambamba na haki za
mlaji.
Mkurugenzi Mkuu amesisitiza kuwa kula njama baina ya washindani kwanza ni
kinyume cha Sheria ya Ushindani na pia kuna athari kubwa kwa mlaji na mtumiaji.
Pia hali hii hufanya makampuni yetu yasiwe shindani kikanda na kimataifa kwani
hukosa ubunifu na ufanisi katika uzalishaji.
Sisi kama Serikali na Wizara inayoongoza na ambayo inasimamia biashara nchini
hatutapenda kuona wafanyabiashara wakila njama ama ya kupanga bei au
kupanga kiasi cha bidhaa cha kuingizwa sokoni kwani ni kinyume na Sheria ya
Ushindani na itakapobainika ni lazima sheria ichukue mkondo wake.
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, Tanzania kupitia utekelezaji wa Dira ya
Maendeleo ya 2025, ilikwisha akisi mwelekeo wa Taifa wa kujenga uchumi imara
na wenye kuhimili ushindani wa kimataifa na kufikia lengo la maisha bora kwa
wote. Kupitia maono haya Serikali ikaanzisha vyombo vya udhibiti wa kisekta
pamoja na Tume ya Ushindani kama sehemu ya kufikia mkakati huu madhubuti ili
kushajiisha ushindani ndani ya nchi na uzingatiwaji wa misingi ya uendeshaji wa
uchumi wa soko.
Kukosekana kwa ushindani katika soko, huduma za ukuaji wa uchumi kwani
wawekezaji wengi hawatavutiwa kuwekeza kwenye masoko yasiyo na ushindani na
matokeo yake ni kulikosesha Taifa fursa za uwekezaji kunakosababisha
kukosekana kwa ajira na mapato kwa njia ya kodi mbalimbali.
Kwa upande mwingine, Kaulimbiu ya siku hii inasisitiza kuwa washindani
wanatakiwa kufanya shughuli zao BILA kula njama baina yao kwani kwa kufanya
hivyo husababisha bei ya bidhaa na huduma kuwa KUBWA pamoja na
kutengeneza UHABA wa bidhaa kwa mlaji jambo ambalo humuathiri mlaji. Jambo
hili husababisha washindani kushindwa kushindana katika masoko ya kikanda na
kimataifa jambo ambalo halileti tija katika uchumi wa nchi.
5

Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, FCC imepata mafanikio makubwa katika
utekelezaji wa Sheria ya Ushindani kama ilivyoelezwa na Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa
FCC.
Ili kuendeleza na kuboresha mafanikio hayo, Serikali imebaini kwamba kuna haja
na hoja za msingi za kuboresha nyenzo muhimu ya kufanikisha usimamizi wa
misingi ya ushindani katika soko na kumlinda mlaji vyema zaidi katika soko.
Nyenzo hiyo ni Sheria ya Ushindani Namba 8 ya mwaka 2003 ambayo kwa sasa
iko katika hatua za mwisho kufanyiwa marekebisho (amendment) ili kuipa nguvu
zaidi ya kushughulikia masuala ya ushindani na kumlinda mlaji.
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, nimesikia changamoto mbalimbali za
kiushindani kutoka kwa wadau kama zilivyoelezewa na Mkurugenzi Mkuu. Sasa
naiagiza FCC kuhakikisha changamoto hizi zinatatuliwa kwa wakati ili kuleta ustawi
katika biashara zetu ikiwa ni pamoja na kusaidia ukuaji wa uchumi. Na hii ndio
sababu inayotufanya tuweke jitihada katika mabadiliko ya sheria ya Ushindani ili
kuhakikisha changamoto zote zinatatuliwa kwa wakati pasipo kukwamishwa na
mapungufu yaliyopo kwenye sheria ya sasa.
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, nihitimishe hotuba yangu kwa kuwataka
wawakilishi wa wadau wafahamu na kuwafikishia ujumbe wenzao ambao
hawajapata fursa ya kuwa nasi pahala hapa kama ifuatavyo;
1. Madhumuni ya Serikali katika kusimamia uchumi wa soko si kukataza biashara
bali kutaka ifanyike kwa kuzingatia sheria na misingi ya ushindani.
2. Washindani wanatakiwa kushindana na si kula njama za kukwepa kushindana
sokoni, ili kutimiza malengo yaliyowekwa na sheria ikiwa ni pamoja na
kuhakikisha wananchi wanapata huduma zenye ubora, wanapata huduma katika
bei nzuri na wanakuwa na wigo mpana wa kuchagua bidhaa na huduma. Haya
yote yatawezekana iwapo tu tutafanya biashara zetu kwa kuzingatia misingi ya
ushindani. Washindani watumie fursa iliyopo kutatua migogoro inayohusu
ushindani baina yao kwa kutumia vyombo husika ambavyo vimewekwa kisheria
kama Tume ya Ushindani (FCC).
6

3. Tume ya Ushindani pamoja na vyombo vingine vinavyosimamia masuala ya
biashara, vitekeleze majukumu yao kwa kuongeza zaidi utoaji wa elimu kwa
wafanyabiashara na kuwaelekeza zaidi kuhusu yawapasayo kutenda ili kuepuka
uvunjwaji wa sheria. Aidha, niwashukuru na kuwapongeza sana wanahabari kwa
kujumuika nasi katika shughuli hii, hakika mnafanya kazi muhimu sana katika
kuuhabarisha Umma juu ya shughuli zinazofanywa na Serikali.
Baada ya kusema hayo, kwa heshima na taadhima, natamka kuwa
Maadhimisho ya Kitaifa ya Siku ya Ushindani Duniani yenye Kaulimbiu “Cartel
and their harmful effect on consumers” yaani “Njama baina ya washindani na
madhara yake kwa walaji na watumiaji” yamehitimishwa rasmi leo tarehe 5
Disemba, 2023.

Speech by Hon. Dr. Ashatu K. Kijaji (MP), Minister for Industry and Trade,
during the World Competition Day Summit held at Serengeti Conference Hall,
Competition House, Dar es Salaam on December 5, 2023.

Director-General of the FCC, Mr. William Erio,
Director-General of the Tanzania Bureau of Standards, Dr. Athuman Y.
Ngenya,
CEO of the Tanzania Investment Centre, Mr. Gilead J. Teri,
CEO of the Business Registration and Licensing Agency (BRELA), Mr.
Godfrey Nyaisa,
Representatives of the East African Community Competition Authority,
Representatives of Trade Marks East Africa (TMEA),
CEO of the Tanzania Communications Regulatory Authority,
7

CEO of the Small Industries Development Organization (SIDO),
CEO of the Weights and Measures Agency (WMA),
CEO of the National Development Corporation (NDC),
CEO of the Tanzania Investment Centre (TIC),
Management and Staff of the Fair Competition Commission,
Representatives from Ministries, Departments, and Government Institutions,
Representatives of small-scale miners from the Lake Zone,
Representatives of seed producers and distributors from the Northern Zone,

Zone,
Representatives of industries and traders from the Southern Highlands Zone,
Representatives of cashew farmers from the Eastern Zone,
Distinguished guests,
Members of the press,
Ladies and Gentlemen,
I have the honour to express my gratitude to the Almighty God, full of mercy and
grace, for granting us good health and enabling us to come together to participate
in this important event commemorating the World Competition Day summit, held
nationally here in Dar es Salaam.
Secondly, I would like to thank the FCC for inviting me to these celebrations. I
commend them for the excellent organization and coordination of this World
Competition Day event. Well done!
Furthermore, I want to sincerely thank all stakeholders and invitees for responding
to the call to attend this crucial culmination of the World Competition Day
celebrations for the year 2023. Despite your other commitments, we appreciate
your presence.
Dear participants and invited guests, we all know that the purpose of any
business is to make and maximize profit. In pursuing this goal, various methods are
employed by businesses, including legitimate methods that promote innovation and
competition, as well as illegitimate methods that violate existing laws, rules, and
regulations. This is a significant challenge that negatively impacts business and the
economy as a whole.
In response to this challenge, the United Nations, through Decision No. 34/447 of
December 19, 1979, adopted the Multilaterally Agreed Equitable Principles and
Rules for the Control of Restrictive Business Practices during its meeting from April
8 to 22, 1980. Since then, these principles have been instrumental in the creation of
competition laws worldwide under the coordination of the United Nations
Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD).
8

This laid the foundation for the establishment of World Competition Day
celebrations to commemorate the efforts to control practices that undermine
competition in global trade, held annually on December 5.
Dear participants and invited guests, practices that undermine competition, the
foundation of global competition law, can be categorized into the following groups:
1. Anti-Competitive Agreements: These include
a. Competitors meeting and fixing prices for goods and services;
b. Competitors agreeing on the quantity of goods produced (output restriction);
c. Competitors refusing to usher products to the market (collective boycott);
d. Competitors agreeing on how to bid when tenders are announced (bid rigging).
2. Abuse/misuse of market power by companies with significant market dominance.
3. Mergers of companies aimed at strengthening market dominance and affecting
competition and consumers in the market.
Dear participants and invited guests, each year during these celebrations, there
is a guiding theme. The theme for 2023 is "Prioritizing Socially Sensitive Sectors,"
which in Tanzania has been interpreted as "Cartels and their harmful effects on
consumers." This theme is timely as the world continues to grapple with the effects
of two major disasters, COVID-19 and the war in Ukraine and Russia, resulting in
rising prices of goods and services. This situation urges businesses to seek ways to
increase profits through various means, including cartels. This could have negative
effects on the nation's economy and hinder the efforts of the sixth-phase
government in achieving sustainable development for its citizens. I take this
opportunity, as the government, to urge businesses to avoid cartels, and the FCC,
as the regulatory authority, to closely monitor market conditions.
Dear participants and invited guests, I have been informed that as part of these
celebrations, the FCC conducted seminars for various stakeholders in the regions it
oversees, including:
(i) Small-scale miners in the Lake Zone;
(ii) Seed producers and distributors from the Northern Zone, Arusha;
(iii) Grape and sunflower oil processors from the FCC headquarters in Dodoma;
(iv) Industries and traders from the Southern Highlands Zone, Mbeya;
(iv) Cashew farmers from the Eastern Zone – Mtwara.
I have also been informed that representatives from each mentioned
region are present here, utilizing this opportunity to learn and witness
firsthand the challenges they face in their areas and how the FCC
addresses them according to existing laws and competition principles.
9

Dear participants and invited guests, competition law plays a crucial role in
building the economy. Conducting our businesses following the principles of
competition will bring the following benefits:
(i) Increased efficiency in the production and distribution of goods and services;
(ii) Promotion of innovation;
(iii) Improved use of resources by focusing on efficiency.
These benefits will enable us to compete in regional and international markets,
especially considering that Tanzania is already part of the African Continental Free
Trade Area (AfCFTA). Therefore, without following these principles, Tanzania may
become a market for products from other countries.
Dear participants and invited guests, I believe you have heard the insightful
details outlined by the Director-General of the FCC regarding the core
responsibilities carried out by the FCC in controlling and overseeing Tanzania's
mainland market to ensure that participants, especially competing businesses and
companies, adhere to competition principles and consumer rights.
The Director-General emphasized that engaging in cartel activities is not only
against competition law but also has significant negative effects on consumers.
Such practices make our companies uncompetitive regionally and internationally,
as they lack innovation and efficiency in production. As the government and the
leading ministry overseeing business in the country, we do not want to see
businesses engaging in price-fixing or controlling the quantity of goods released to
the market because it is against competition law, and when detected, legal action
will be taken.
Dear participants and invited guests, through the implementation of the Vision
2025 Development Plan, Tanzania has already set the direction to build a robust
and internationally competitive economy, aiming to achieve a better quality of life
for all. In line with these aspirations, the government established sectoral regulatory
bodies, including the Fair Competition Commission, as part of a comprehensive
strategy to promote competition within the country and adhere to the principles of a
market economy.
The absence of competition in the market hinders economic growth, as many
investors are not attracted to invest in non-competitive markets. This leads to
missed investment opportunities, resulting in a lack of employment opportunities
and revenue through various taxes.

conduct their business without conspiring against each other. Engaging in such
conspiracies leads to higher prices of goods and services and creates a shortage of
products for consumers, adversely affecting them. This situation prevents
10

competitors from competing regionally and internationally, which is not beneficial to
the country's economy.

in implementing the Competition Act, as outlined by the Director-General of the
FCC.

need and valid reasons to improve the essential tools for implementing competition
principles in the market and better-protecting consumers. This tool is the
Competition Act No. 8 of 2003, which is currently in the final stages of being
amended to give it more power to address competition issues and protect
consumers.

challenges from stakeholders, as explained by the Director-General. I now instruct
the FCC to ensure that these challenges are addressed promptly to promote
prosperity in our businesses and contribute to economic growth. This is why we are
investing efforts in amending the Competition Act to ensure that all challenges are
resolved without being hindered by the shortcomings in the current law.

representatives of stakeholders to understand and convey the message to their
colleagues who did not have the opportunity to be with us today:

business but to ensure that it operates in accordance with the law and competition
principles.

the available opportunities to resolve disputes related to competition using the
appropriate legal channels, such as the Fair Competition Commission (FCC).

consumers" have officially winded up today, December 5, 2023.

Mheshimiwa Rosemary Sinyamule, Mkuu wa Mkoa wa Dodoma,
Mheshimiwa Dkt. Hashil Abdallah, Katibu Mkuu, Wizara ya Uwekezaji,
Viwanda na Biashara,

ya Viwanda, Biashara, Kilimo na Mifugo,

Wafanyabiashara,
Wawakilishi kutoka Wizara, Taasisi, Idara za Serikali na Mamlaka za Tawala za
Mikoa na Wilaya,
Wawakilishi kutoka Taasisi za Ushauri wa Kisheria na Vyama vya Uwakilishi
wa Watumiaji,
1

Menejimenti na Wafanyakazi wa FCC,
Waandishi wa Habari,
Mabibi na Mabwana
Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania!
Awali ya yote napenda kutumia fursa hii kumshukuru Mwenyezi Mungu mwingi wa
rehema kwa kutuamsha salama tukiwa na afya njema na kutuwezesha kushiriki
katika maadhimisho haya adhimu. Napenda pia kuushukuru uongozi wa Tume ya
Ushindani (FCC) kwa kunialika kuwa mgeni rasmi katika maadhimisho haya.
Aidha, nitumie fursa hii kuwashukuru wadau wote walioitikia wito wa kushiriki katika
maadhimisho haya muhimu wakiwemo uongozi wa Mkoa wa Dodoma chini ya
Mheshimiwa Mkuu wa Mkoa, Waheshimiwa Wajumbe wa Kamati ya Kudumu ya
Bunge ya Viwanda, Biashara, Kilimo na Mifugo wakiongozwa na Mheshimiwa
David Mwakiposa Khenzile (Mb), Wadau wa maendeleo, wamiliki wa Alama za
Biashara, vyama vya uwakilishi wa watumiaji na wanafunzi kutoka vyuo vya elimu
ya juu na wadau wote mliopo hapa kwa kutenga muda wenu na kuhudhuria
kongamano hili.
Pia nimefurahishwa kufahamu kuwa wawakilishi wa wafanyabiashara, wazalishaji,
wawakilishi kutoka chama cha Mawakala wa Ushuru wa Forodha, Vyombo vya
Serikali vya usimamizi wa soko na uwezeshaji kibiashara pamoja na wamiliki wa
Alama za Biashara ni miongoni mwa washiriki wa Kongamano hili ambalo
linaadhimishwa chini ya kauli mbiu “Kukuza Ubia Kati ya Sekta ya Umma na
Binafsi katika Kudhibiti Bidhaa Bandia”.
Waswahili wanasema mtu akikualika amekuheshimu, lakini akiitikia wito
amekuheshimu zaidi. Hivyo, tunapenda kuwashukuru kwa heshima hii mliyotupatia
ya kujumuika nasi.
2

Mwitikio wenu mkubwa wa mahudhurio katika kongamano hili la leo ni faraja katika
Wizara yangu, mkiakisi kwamba wadau wote mnakerwa na kuumizwa na biashara
ya bidhaa bandia. Hivyo, ni dhahiri kwamba mpo tayari kushirikiana na Serikali na
Taasisi yetu ya FCC katika mapambano dhidi ya bidhaa bandia kama inavyosema
kauli mbiu ya maadhimisho haya.
Wakati nilipopata mwaliko wa FCC wa kushiriki katika Maadhimisho haya, sikusita
hata kidogo kuitikia wito huo kwa kuwa suala hili la kupambana na bidhaa bandia ni
la muhimu sana katika kuhakikisha kuwa Wizara yangu ambayo inashughulikia
Uwekezaji, Viwanda na Biashara, inatekeleza majukumu yake kwa ufanisi.
Bidhaa Bandia zinaathiri uwekezaji kwa kuwa wawekezaji wanavutiwa zaidi
kuwekeza katika nchi zenye mifumo thabiti ya udhibiti (regulatory regimes)
zinazoonesha juhudi za wazi za kudhibiti bidhaa bandia, wakiamini kuwa uwekezaji
wao utalipa. Kama sote tunavyofahamu, kuvutia uwekezaji kutoka nje (Foreign
Direct Investment) ni muhimu sana katika kuleta maendeleo ya kiuchumi katika
nchi yoyote duniani, ikiwemo Tanzania. Ni Dhahiri basi kwamba udhibiti wa bidhaa
bandia ni kichocheo cha kuvutia wawekezaji zaidi hapa nchini, kama inavyoonesha
katika takwimu za Kituo cha Uwekezaji Nchini (TIC).
Wizara yangu pia inashughulika na viwanda vinavyozalisha bidhaa kwa nia ya
kuziuza ndani na nje ya mipaka yetu. Kudhibiti bidhaa bandia kwa ufanisi
kunaongeza soko la bidhaa zinazozalishwa katika viwanda na hivyo kuchochea
viwanda vilivyopo kuongeza uzalishaji na viwanda vipya kuanzishwa.
Kuongezeka kwa uzalishaji katika viwanda kutakuza ajira, kutaongeza mapato kwa
njia ya kodi na kuongeza urahisi wa upatikanaji wa bidhaa kwa bei nafuu
(affordable) kutokana na kuongezeka kwa ushindani katika soko.
3

Udhibiti mzuri wa biashara ya bidhaa bandia pia utasaidia kushamirisha biashara
ya kiushindani na itaiwezesha nchi yetu kutumia fursa za masoko ya kikanda, Soko
Huru la Afrika (AcFTA) na Masoko ya Kimataifa.
Katika kutekeleza haya ni dhahiri kwamba ushirikiano madhubuti na wa karibu wa
sekta binafsi na sekta ya Umma ni muhimu kuwepo kutokana na ukweli kwamba
wadau wa shughuli za uwekezaji, viwanda na biashara wanatoka katika sekta
binafsi na vyombo vya Serikali ndivyo vinavyotengeneza mazingira wezeshi katika
soko kwa utendaji wa ufanisi wa kibiashara ikiwemo udhibiti wa bidhaa bandia.
Serikali inapenda kuona kuwa udhibiti wa bidhaa bandia unafanyika kwa ufanisi
zaidi kwa juhudi za pamoja za wadau wote wa biashara.
Serikali inatambua na inapongeza juhudi za FCC katika kudhibiti bidhaa bandia.
Takwimu zinaonesha kuwa kiwango cha bidhaa bandia zinaoingia nchini ni kidogo.
Mathalan, katika miezi tisa ya kwanza ya mwaka wa fedha 2022/2023, FCC
ilikagua makasha ya kusafirishia mizigo (containers) 7918 katika Bandari ya Dar es
Salaam, ambapo kati ya hayo makasha 206 tu, sawa na asilimia 2.6, yalikutwa
yakiwa na shehena ya bidhaa zinazokiuka Sheria ya Alama za Bidhaa. Hii
inamaanisha kuwa asilimia 97.4 ya bidhaa zote zilizokaguliwa katika kipindi hicho,
zilikidhi matakwa ya Sheria ya Alama za Bidhaa na hivyo kuwa bidhaa halali.
Takwimu hizi zinaonesha wazi kuwa FCC kwa kushirikiana na vyombo vingine vya
Serikali na waagizaji na wazalishaji wa bidhaa mbalimbali wanafanya kazi nzuri na
kuifanya nchi yetu kuwa ni sehemu nzuri ya kuwekeza kwa nia ya kuzalisha bidhaa
mbalimbali, sehemu nzuri ya kufanya biashara na kujenga viwanda.
Pamoja na mafanikio haya, ni dhahiri kwamba kuongezeka kwa ushirikiano kati ya
FCC na wadau wake kutafanya udhibiti dhidi ya bidhaa bandia kuwa ya mafanikio
zaidi. Aina hizi za ushirikiano ni pamoja na:
4

1. kuongeza ushirikiano katika kutoa elimu kwa wadau kuhusu madhara ya
bidhaa bandia na jinsi ya kuzitambua,
2. Waagizaji wakubwa wakubwa wa bidhaa kutoingiza nchini bidhaa bandia;
3. Wakala wa Ushuru wa Forodha kutokukubali kusafirisha na kuingiza bidhaa
bandia;
4. Balozi za nchi ambazo bidhaa zake zinapita katika nchi ya Tanzania kwa
kushirikiana na mamlaka husika katika nchi zao kuwaelimisha
wafanyabiashara wao kutokuagiza na kupitisha bidhaa bandia nchini
Tanzania
5. Mashirika ya Kimataifa na Asasi mbalimbali za uwezeshaji wa kibiashara
kuisaidia FCC katika kupata mafunzo na nyenzo za kisasa za kutambua na
kudhibiti bidhaa bandia;
6. Kuuelimisha Umma kuhusu madhara ya bidhaa bandia na hivyo kuwashauri
waepuke kuzinunua;
Serikali kwa upande wake, kupitia Wizara, itasimamia ukamilishaji wa maboresho
ya Sheria ya Alama za Bidhaa katika kuunga mkono juhudi hizo na kuleta ufanisi
zaidi kiutendaji.
Natambua kuwa FCC kwa muda mrefu ilikuwa imejikita zaidi katika kaguzi kwenye
bandari ya Dar es Salaam pamoja na bandari zake kavu zipatazo 15. Eneo la
ukaguzi kwa sasa linaongezeka ambapo kutakuwa na Bandari Kavu ya Kwala,
Mkoani Pwani, pamoja na vituo vya ukaguzi wa pamoja mipakani (OSBPs)
vilivyojengwa na vinavyoendelea kujengwa kwa uratibu wa Jumuiya ya Afrika
Mashariki kupitia Mradi wa Uboreshaji wa Biashara na Usafirishaji (East African
Trade and Transport Facilitation Project -EATTFP), kwa ufadhili wa Taasisi ya
TradeMark East Africa (TMEA), Benki ya Maendeleo ya Afrika (AfDB), Benki ya
Dunia na Shirika la Maendeleo la Ushirikiano la Japan (JICA).
5

Kwakuwa FCC imeshaanzisha ofisi za Kanda katika Miji ya Mwanza, Arusha na
Mbeya, naielekeza iongeze juhudi katika kufanya kaguzi za bidhaa bandia katika
maeneo ya mipakani na Kanda hizo. Serikali inakaribisha uungwaji mkono wa
wadau katika kuiwezesha FCC katika kufanikisha utendaji wa ofisi hizo kwa ufanisi.
Ndugu Washiriki
Kwa mujibu wa ratiba ya kongamano la leo, mada mbalimbali zitawasilishwa na
kujadiliwa. Ni matumaini yangu kuwa zitakuwa zinajadiliwa kwa kina na kutolewa
mapendekezo ya namna bora ya kuboresha uhusiano kati ya sekta ya Umma na
binafsi katika kudhibiti bidhaa bandia katika maeneo yaliyoainishwa kwenye mada
na maeneo mengine kwa ujumla.
Baada ya kusema hayo nawatakiwa mkutano mwema
Sasa ninayo furaha kutamka kuwa Kongamano hili la Kilele cha Maadhimisho ya
Kitaifa ya Siku ya Udhibiti wa Bidhaa Duniani, limefunguliwa rasmi.
Asanteni kwa kunisikiliza.
Mhe. Dr. Ashatu K. Kijaji (Mb)
Waziri wa Uwekezaji, Viwanda na Biashara

Ladies and Gentlemen,
I would like to use this opportunity to thank the Almighty God for enabling us to
participate in these significant celebrations. I therefore, would like to express my
gratitude to the leadership of the Fair Competition Commission (FCC) for inviting
me to be the esteemed guest at these celebrations.
I extend my appreciation to all stakeholders who responded to the call to participate
in these important celebrations, including the Dodoma Regional leadership under
the Regional Commissioner, members of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on
7

Industry, Trade, Agriculture, and Livestock led by Honorable David Mwakiposa
Khenzile (MP), development partners, Ambassadors from various countries, brand
owners, consumer representation associations, and students from higher education
institutions, among others, for taking the time to attend this conference.
I am also pleased to learn that representatives from traders, producers,
representatives from the Customs Agents Association, Government market
management and trade facilitation agencies, as well as brand owners, are among
the participants in this conference.
As the Swahili saying goes, when someone invites you, they respect you, but when
you respond to the invitation, you show even greater respect. Therefore, we thank
you for the value you have shown us by joining us.
Your significant response in attendance at this summit is a source of
encouragement for my ministry, reflecting that all stakeholders are concerned and
affected by the trade in counterfeit goods. It is clear that you are ready to
collaborate with the government and FCC in the fight against counterfeit goods, as
emphasized by the theme of these celebrations.
When I received the FCC's invitation to participate in these celebrations, I did not
hesitate at all to respond to that call because the issue of combating counterfeit
goods is crucial in ensuring that my ministry, which deals with Industry and Trade,
performs its duties efficiently.
Counterfeit goods affect Industry, Trade and investment as well because investors
are more attracted to invest in countries with robust regulatory regimes that show
clear efforts to control counterfeit goods, believing that their investment will pay off.
As we all know, attracting foreign direct investment is crucial for economic
development in any country, including Tanzania. It is clear, therefore, that effective
control of counterfeit goods is a catalyst for attracting more investors to our country,
as reflected in the statistics from the Tanzania Investment Center (TIC).
8

My ministry is also responsible for industries that produce goods for sale within and
outside our borders. Effective control of counterfeit goods increases the market for
products manufactured in industries, thus stimulating existing industries to increase
production and new industries to be established.

through taxes, and make it easier for consumers to access affordable goods due to

HOTUBA YA MWENYEKITI WA FCC WAKATI WA UFUNGUZI WA
SEMINA YA MASUALA YA USHINDANI, KUMLINDA MLAJI NA
UDHIBITI WA BIDHAA BANDIA KWA WAHARIRI WA HABARI ZA
BIASHARA NA UCHUMI KATIKA OFISI YA FCC JIJINI DAR ES
SALAAM TAREHE 13 APRILI, 2023.
Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa FCC,
Mwenyekiti wa Jukwaa la Wahariri,
Mjumbe wa Kamati tendaji ya Jukwaa la Wahariri,
Wafanyakazi wa FCC,
Wahariri wa vyombo mbalimbali vya habari,
Waandishi wa habari waandamizi kutoka vyombo mbalimbali vya
habari,
Wanahabari,
Wageni waalikwa,
Mabibi na Mabwana.
Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania!
Naomba nianze kwa kumshukuru Mwenyezi Mungu mwingi wa
rehema na fadhili kwa kutuwezesha kukutana siku hii tukiwa wazima
na wenye afya njema. Aidha, nitumie fursa hii kuwashukuru ninyi
nyote kwa dhati kabisa kwa kuitikia wito wetu na kujitokeza kwa wingi
kujumuika nasi katika semina hii, ni dhahiri mmeamua kuipa
umuhimu shughuli inayohusu sekta ya habari na majukumu yetu ya
kitaasisi kwa maslahi mapana ya mlaji. Hivyo basi, kwa niaba ya
1

watumishi wenzangu wa Tume ya Ushindani nawashukuru sana kwa
kuja kushiriki nasi katika semina hii fupi.
Tumeamua kufanya semina hii kwa madhumuni makubwa mawili;
Kwanza, kwa kutambua umuhimu wenu na nafasi zenu katika
vyombo vya habari kama wahariri na waandishi waandamizi wa
habari, sisi FCC ndio shughuli yetu hiyo, kwahiyo tulidhani kwanza
kuwajengea uwezo na kuwaongezea uelewa wenu wa shughuli za
biashara na uchumi ambazo FCC tunazisimamia kwa karibu, na
tunafikiri kwamba baada ya kumaliza mkutano huu tutakuwa
tumefanikiwa kwa kiwango kikubwa katika kufanikisha hilo.
Pili, tunataka kupitia kwenu kuujulisha Umma wa watanzania kuhusu
shughuli mbalimbali zinazohusiana na FCC na kwa namna gani
wanaweza kuzitumia katika kupata huduma stahiki kama ambavyo
wanazilipia, kwamba kile wanachokipata ndicho walichostahili
kukipata.
Katika mkutano wetu wa leo, nitaeleza kwa kifupi majukumu ya FCC,
wenzangu wataeleza kwa kina lakini kimsingi shughuli zetu kubwa ni
mbili;
Kwanza, ni kukuza na kulinda Ushindani wa kibiashara hapa nchini
na si kuzuia. Katika kulinda kama mnavyojua nchi yetu ya Tanzania
iliingia katika mfumo wa uchumi wa biashara huria tangu mwaka
1980, biashara huria haimaanishi watu wafanye mambo kiholela kwa
kufanya vurugu, wao wenyewe kwa wenyewe kuhujumiana lakini
2

kuhakikisha kwamba pia wanapata faida kubwa iwezekanavyo wakati
mwingine kwa kumtesa mlaji.
Sisi kama FCC kazi yetu ni kuratibu na kuangalia shughuli hizi kwa
karibu ili kuhakikisha kwamba chochote kinachofanywa hakikiuki
misingi ya ushindani na kila aliyeingia katika soko la ushindani wa
biashara basi anapata matunda ya kile kinachostahiki na faida
aliyoitegemea kwa kufanya biashara katika misingi ya haki na sahihi.
Pamoja na kukuza na kulinda shughuli za biashara katika nchi yetu,
pia tuna jukumu la kumlinda mlaji wa shughuli hizo za biashara
ambapo ndio sehemu kubwa ya watanzania ambao ndio wapiga kura
wanaoiweka Serikali madarakani. Kazi yetu ni kuahakikisha wapiga
kura au wananchi hao wanapata matarajio waliyoyakusudia na kile
ambacho wanakipata kinawaonesha kwamba kweli Serikali yao
imewajali na wanapata vitu ambavyo ni sahihi.
Sasa na hilo nalo ni kazi yetu kwasababu wafanyabiashara kwa hulka
yao na ndio maana ya biashara, kazi yao kubwa ni kupata faida, faida
hiyo inaweza kupatikana kwa njia zisizo halali au kwa njia halali ama
wakati mwingine kwa njia za kupigana vita, kuhujumiana wenyewe
kwa wenyewe, kuhujumiana kati yao na walaji na wasambazaji wa
kati, kwahiyo hapo ndipo FCC tunahakikisha mambo hayo
hayajitokezi na biashara zinashamiri ili kuwavutia wawekezaji katika
nchi yetu.
Sasa hayo ndio mtakayosikia kwetu, matumaini yetu kuwa
mtakapotoka katika semina hii na uelewa mtakaokuwa nao, basi
kupitia vyombo vyenu naamini mtatoa elimu stahiki kwa watanzania ili
3

baadaye sisi na ninyi kwa pamoja tuweze kuhakikisha kwamba
uendeshaji wa shughuli za biashara unakuwa wa haki na unazingatia
misingi iliyokubalika kwa mujibu wa sheria, kanuni na taratibu za
kufanya biashara katika soko la huria.
Ndugu wahariri, kupitia mkutano wetu wa leo mtapata mada tatu, ya
kwanza itakuwa udhibiti wa bidhaa bandia, ni dhahiri ninyi nyote
mnafahamu Serikali ya awamu ya sita imejikita katika kuhimiza
wawekezaji ili waje kuwekeza katika nchi yetu, sasa kunapokuwa na
uwekezaji hususan katika sekta ya viwanda na uzalishaji lazima uwe
na uhakika kwamba kwanza uwekezaji ule utakupa faida
unayostahili, na kufanya hivyo lazima mazingira ya kufanya biashara
katika nchi yetu yawe salama na yanazingatia kanuni za kibiashara
za kimataifa. Kwahiyo, sisi FCC tunafanya hilo ili kuwavutia
wawekezaji zaidi na wale ambao tayari wapo kuhakikisha kwamba
wanafanya biashara bila kubugudhiwa kwa namna yoyote ile na
washindani wenzao, lakini pia wanapata huduma wanazostahiki
kuwawezesha kufanya biashara kwa wakati.
Hivyo basi, FCC tunataka kuangalia hilo lakini pia hatuwezi kufanya
hilo kama tutaruhusu kushamiri kwa bidhaa bandia.
Aidha, katika semina hii mtaelezwa pia masuala ya bidhaa bandia
kwa maana ya dhana, aina, utambuzi na athari zake katika uchumi
wa nchi yetu. Sasa hayo yote yanakwenda kwa pamoja katika
kuimarisha biashara ya ushindani na kuhakikisha bidhaa bandia
haziingii nchini au hazizalishwi na hivyo kuzuia uwekezaji usifanikiwe
4

lakini pia kumlinda mwekezaji dhidi ya athari zinazoweza kutokana na
hali hiyo.
Ndugu wahariri, naomba nitumie fursa hii kuwafahamisha kuwa
sasa FCC tumefungua ofisi za Kanda ya Ziwa Mwanza iliyopo katika
jengo la PSSSF, ghorofa ya pili, barabara ya Kenyatta, Kanda ya
Kaskazini Arusha iliyopo AICC, jengo la Serengeti ghorofa ya tano
pamoja na Kanda ya Nyanda za Juu Kusini Mbeya iliyopo katika
jengo la NSSF ghorofa ya chini, mtaa wa Sisimba barabara ya
Karume. Lengo kuu la ufunguzi wa ofisi hizi ni kusogeza huduma
karibu na wananchi, hivyo ni rai yangu kwenu kutumia weredi na
nyenzo za kitaaluma mlizonazo kutusaidia kuujulisha Umma wa
Tanzania uwepo wa ofisi hizi sanjali na mjukumu tunayoyatekeleza
kwa mujibu wa sheria.
Baada ya kusema hayo, nimalizie kwa kuwasihi sana kuendelea
kuzingatia weledi na maadili ya taaluma yenu katika kuwahudumia
watanzania na wadau wote wa maendeleo ili kwa pamoja kuunga
mkono jitihada zinazofanywa na Serikali katika kuleta maendeleo
katika Taifa letu.
Nawatakia Semina njema na sasa natamka kuwa Semina hii
imefunguliwa rasmi.
Asanteni sana kwa kunisikiliza!
Speech by the Chairman of the Fair Competition Commission (FCC)
during the opening of the Seminar on Competition Issues, Consumer
Protection, and Control of Counterfeit Goods for Business and
5

Economic Editors at the FCC Offices in Dar es Salaam on April 13,
2023.
Director-General of the FCC,
Chairman of the Editors' Forum,
Member of the Executive Committee of the Editors' Forum,
FCC Staff,
Editors from various media outlets,
Senior journalists from various media outlets,
Journalists,
Invited Guests,
Ladies and Gentlemen.
I would like to extend the Almighty God, full of mercy and grace, for
enabling us to meet on this day in good health. I also want to
sincerely thank all of you for responding to our invitation and turning
out in large numbers to join us in this seminar. It is evident that you
have decided to give importance to activities related to the media
sector and our institutional responsibilities for the broader benefit of
consumers. Therefore, on behalf of my fellow staff at the Fair
Competition Commission, I express my sincere gratitude for your
active participation in this short seminar.
6

We have decided to hold this seminar with two main purposes;
First, recognizing your importance and roles in the media as editors
and senior journalists, our role at the FCC is to closely monitor these
activities. Therefore, we thought it wise to first enhance your capacity
and increase your understanding of business and economic activities
that the FCC closely oversees. We believe that, after completing this
meeting, we will have achieved significant success in that regard.
Second, you as a bridge for information, we want to inform the
Tanzanian public about various activities related to the FCC and how
they can utilize them to receive appropriate services as they pay for
them. What they receive should reflect what they are entitled to.
In our meeting today, I will briefly explain the responsibilities of the
FCC, while my colleagues will delve deeper. In essence, our major
tasks are two-fold;
Firstly, to promote and protect fair competition in the country, not to
hinder it. As you know, our country, Tanzania, entered the free-
market economic system in 1980. Free trade does not mean people
should engage in chaotic and disruptive activities, undermining each
other and causing harm. It means ensuring that everyone benefits as
much as possible while conducting business. As the FCC, our task is
to coordinate and closely monitor these activities to ensure that
nothing violates the principles of competition. Every participant in the
business competition should reap the fruits they deserve, engaging in
fair and just trade.
7

Alongside promoting and protecting business activities in our country,
we also have the responsibility to protect the consumers of these
business activities. They constitute the majority of Tanzanians, the
same individuals who vote to put the government in power. Our role
is to ensure that voters or citizens receive the benefits they intended
and that what they receive shows that their government cares and
provides them with what is right.
This is our responsibility because, by their nature, businesspeople,
being in business, are primarily focused on making a profit. This profit
can be obtained through both legal and illegal means, sometimes
through unethical means such as harming the consumer. Therefore,
the FCC ensures that these things do not happen, ensuring that
business thrives to attract more investors to our country.
Now, that is what you will hear from us. We hope that when you leave
this seminar with the knowledge you have gained, you will use your
platforms to educate Tanzanians so that together we can ensure that
business operations are fair and adhere to the accepted principles
according to the laws, regulations, and procedures of conducting
business in a free-market.
Dear Editors, through today's meeting, you will have three main
topics. The first will be the combat against counterfeit goods. It is
clear to all of you that the Sixth Phase Government is committed to
encouraging investors to come and invest in our country. Now, when
there is investment, especially in the industrial and production
sectors, you must be sure that the investment will yield the expected
8

profit. To achieve this, the business environment in our country must
be safe and adhere to international business principles. Therefore,
we, at the FCC, work towards this goal to attract more investors and
ensure that existing ones can conduct business without disturbance
from their competitors. However, we also need to prevent the
proliferation of counterfeit goods.
In this seminar, you will also be informed about counterfeit goods in
terms of concepts, types, identification, and their effects on our
country's economy. All these efforts go hand in hand in strengthening
competitive trade and ensuring that counterfeit goods do not enter or
are produced in the country, thereby preventing the failure of
investments and protecting investors from potential harm.
Dear Editors, I would like to take this opportunity to inform you that
the FCC has opened offices in the Lake Zone in Mwanza, located in
the PSSSF building, second floor, Kenyatta Road. In the Northern
Zone, we have an office in Arusha at AICC, Serengeti building, fifth
floor. Additionally, in the Southern Highlands Zone in Mbeya, our
office is located in the NSSF building, ground floor, Sisimba Street,
Karume Road. The main purpose of opening these offices is to bring
services closer to the people. Therefore, I urge you to use your
expertise and professional tools to help us inform the Tanzanian
public about the existence of these offices and the responsibilities we
carry out in accordance with the law.
After saying that, I would like to conclude by urging you to continue
adhering to professionalism and ethical standards in your profession
9

as you serve Tanzanians and all development stakeholders. Let us,
together, support the efforts made by the government to bring
development to our nation.
I wish you a successful seminar, and I now declare this seminar
officially open.
Thank you very much for listening!

encouraging investors to come and invest in our country. Now, when
there is investment, especially in the industrial and production
sectors, you must be sure that the investment will yield the expected
8profit. To achieve this, the business environment in our country must
be safe and adhere to international business principles. Therefore,
we, at the FCC, work towards this goal to attract more investors and
ensure that existing ones can conduct business without disturbance
from their competitors. However, we also need to prevent the
proliferation of counterfeit goods.
In this seminar, you will also be informed about counterfeit goods in
terms of concepts, types, identification, and their effects on our
country's economy. All these efforts go hand in hand in strengthening
competitive trade and ensuring that counterfeit goods do not enter or
are produced in the country, thereby preventing the failure of
investments and protecting investors from potential harm.
Dear Editors, I would like to take this opportunity to inform you that
the FCC has opened offices in the Lake Zone in Mwanza, located in
the PSSSF building, second floor, Kenyatta Road. In the Northern
Zone, we have an office in Arusha at AICC, Serengeti building, fifth
floor. Additionally, in the Southern Highlands Zone in Mbeya, our
office is located in the NSSF building, ground floor, Sisimba Street,
Karume Road. The main purpose of opening these offices is to bring
services closer to the people. Therefore, I urge you to use your
expertise and professional tools to help us inform the Tanzanian
public about the existence of these offices and the responsibilities we
carry out in accordance with the law.
After saying that, I would like to conclude by urging you to continue
adhering to professionalism and ethical standards in your profession
9as you serve Tanzanians and all development stakeholders. Let us,
together, support the efforts made by the government to bring
development to our nation.
I wish you a successful seminar, and I now declare this seminar
officially open.
Thank you very much for listening!

text:
HOTUBA YA MKUU WA MKOA WA ARUSHA WAKATI WA
UFUNGUZI WA SEMINA YA UHAMASISHAJI WA MASUALA YA
USHINDANI, UDHIBITI WA BIDHAA BANDIA NA KUMLINDA
MLAJI KWA WAZALISHAJI KATIKA UKUMBI WA OFISI YA
MKUU WA MKOA WA ARUSHA JIJINI ARUSHA TAREHE 23
FEBRUARI, 2023.
Mwakilishi wa Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa Tume ya Ushindani (FCC),
Mwenyekiti wa CTI Mkoa wa Arusha,
Wazalishaji (CTI),
Watendaji wa FCC,
Afisa Biashara kutoka Sekretarieti ya Mkoa wa Arusha,
Wanahabari,
Wageni waalikwa,
Mabibi na Mabwana.
Jamhuri ya Muungano!
Awali ya yote namshukuru Mwenyezi Mungu mwingi wa rehema na
fadhili kwa kutuwezesha kukutana katika shughuli hii tukiwa wazima
na wenye afya njema. Aidha, nitumie fursa hii kuwakaribisha sana
FCC, CTI na wageni wote mliotoka nje ya Mkoa wa Arusha, Karibuni
sana!
Serikali ya Mkoa wa Arusha ipo imara na tunawahakikishia ulinzi na
usalama pamoja na ushirikiano wa dhati katika shughuli za ujenzi wa
Taifa letu wakati wote mtakapokuwa hapa Arusha.
1

Kipekee nitumie fursa hii pia kuishukuru na kuipongeza Serikali ya
awamu ya sita inayoongozwa na Mhe. Dkt. Samia Suluhu Hassan,
Rais wa Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania, kwa jitihada kubwa
inazozifanya katika kuwaletea maendeleo watanzania wote ikiwa ni
pamoja na kuongeza tija zaidi katika Sekta ya Viwanda na Biashara
ikiwa ni pamoja na masuala ya Ushindani kwa ujumla.
Aidha, nawapongeza sana FCC kwa utekelezaji wa majukumu yenu
kwa mujibu wa Sheria hususan katika masuala ya ushindani, udhibiti
wa bidhaa bandia na kumlinda mlaji kwa ujumla. Haya ni masuala
muhimu sana, endapo tukishirikiana kwa dhati kuyasimamia vizuri na
kwa kuzingatia misingi ya Sheria, hapana shaka Sekta hii ya viwanda
na biashara itastawi na itaongeza tija zaidi katika nchi yetu.
Ndugu wanasemina, leo tumekusanyika mahali hapa kwa lengo kuu
la kupatiwa mafunzo yanayohusu majukumu ya Tume ya Ushindani,
Sheria ya Ushindani, udhibiti wa bidhaa bandia pamoja na wajibu wa
wazalishaji katika kumlinda mlaji. Nawashukuru sana FCC kwa kuona
umuhimu wa kutuletea semina hii katika Mkoa wetu wa Arusha. Ni
dhahiri mmefanya uamuzi sahihi kutokana na Mkoa wetu kuwa na
shughuli nyingi za uzalishaji, utalii na uchumi pia.
Aidha, nawapongeza sana FCC kwa hatua mnazochukua katika
kufanya semina hizi kwa lengo la kuwafikia watanzania wengi zaidi,
lakini bado mna kazi ya ziada katika kuhakikisha mnafanya semina
nyingi zaidi ili watanzania wenzetu ambao wengi wao ni wakulima,
wafanyabiashara na wazalishaji pia wanapata elimu za namna hii
kikamilifu ili kujiweka katika mazingira mazuri ya kiushindani kwa
2

mujibu wa taratibu na kanuni zilizopo. Serikali ya Mkoa wa Arusha
tutashirikiana nanyi kama ambavyo Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa FCC
amebainisha.
Ndugu wanasemina, nimefarijika sana kuona muitikio wenu mzuri
ambapo ninyi ndio wazalishaji, na mna umuhimu mkubwa sana katika
mstakabali wa ukuaji wa uchumi kuanzia ngazi ya kaya hadi Taifa. Ili
muweze kustawi katika shughuli zenu hamna budi kuzingatia taratibu
za nchi na kuzingatia misingi ya Ushindani. Hii ndio sababu ya FCC
kuona umuhimu wa kufanya semina hizi kwenu, hivyo, mna wajibu
wa kutumia fursa hii kwa umakini mkubwa ili baada ya mafunzo haya
tuone mabadiliko chanya yatakayokuwa na tija katika shughuli zenu
za uzalishaji na katika ngazi ya Taifa kwa ujumla.
Wanufaika wa semina ya leo ni wazalishaji, hivyo nitoe rai kwa
taasisi, asasi na wananchi wengine wanaojishughulisha na masuala
ya Ushindani kujenga utamaduni wa kutafuta elimu kwa kina kutoka
FCC na Idara nyingine za Serikali ikiwa ni pamoja na Shirika la
Viwanda Vidogo (SIDO), Shirika la Viwango Tanzania (TBS), Wakala
wa Usajili na Leseni za Biashara (BRELA), na Wakala wa Vipimo
(WMA). Msingi wa kutoa rai hii ni kwasababu Taasisi hizi ikiwa ni
pamoja na FCC ni vyombo muhimu katika ustawi wa biashara na
usimamizi wa soko nchini Tanzania, na endapo Taasisi hizi
zikitumiwa ipasavyo ni dhahiri tija katika kuanzisha, kulea na kukuza
biashara zenu itakuwa kubwa na ya kuridhisha.
Hivyobasi, kupitia Semina hii natoa maelekezo kwa Wakurugenzi wa
Halmashauri zote katika Mkoa wa Arusha kuhakikisha mnayabaini
3

makundi au vikundi ambavyo vinajihusisha na uzalishaji na
vinahudumiwa na Serikali kupitia Halmashauri zenu, hakikisheni
makundi hayo yanapata semina za namna hii ili kuongeza tija na
mnyororo wa thamani katika utekelezaji wa shughuli zao, na suala hili
litafanikiwa kwa kujenga ushirikiano wa kiutendaji na Taasisi hizo za
Serikali ikiwa ni pamoja na FCC ambayo kimsingi inafanya kazi nzuri
sana katika utoaji wa elimu kwa wadau mbalimbali wa maendeleo na
Umma kwa ujumla, pia inafanya kazi vizuri ya udhibiti wa bidhaa
bandia nchini kwa kufanya kaguzi katika maeneo mbalimbali ya nchi
pamoja maingilio ya bidhaa. kwa kushirikiana na Taasisi hizi naamini
shughuli za uzalishaji mali na uchumi kwa wananchi wetu vijijini na
hata mijini utakuwa salama na wenye tija kwa ajili ya maendeleo ya
wananchi wetu.
Hivyo basi, Wakurugenzi wote wa Mamlaka za Serikali za Mitaa
katika Mkoa wa Arusha hakikisheni mnakuwa na mpango kazi mzuri
utakaosaidia kuratibu mafunzo ya namna hii kwa ajili ya makundi yote
yanayonufaika na mikopo au fedha za Serikali zinazowagusa
wanawake, vijana na wenye ulemavu ambapo ni dhahiri
yatawajengea uwezo na weledi katika nyanja za uzalishaji, uuzaji,
ununuzi, utambuzi wa bidhaa bandia ikiwa ni pamoja na kujua misingi
bora ya ushindani wa soko na uchumi kwa ujumla. Aidha, utekelezaji
wa mpango kazi huo uzingatie kuzihusisha taasisi kama FCC katika
utoaji wa elimu.
Ndugu wanasemina, kupitia semina hii mtapokea mada mbalimbali
zitakazowajenga na kuwapa misingi muhimu juu ya biashara na
4

uchumi na mengine mengi yanayoakisi maendeleo katika shughuli
zenu za kila siku.
Hivyo ni vyema mkazingatia kwa makini fursa ya mafunzo haya ili
baada ya mafunzo haya tuone mabadiliko ikiwa ni pamoja na
kuzingatia maadili ya biashara ili kuhakikisha soko linabaki shindani,
bidhaa zinazopelekwa sokoni zinakidhi matarajio ya watumiaji au
wateja na taratibu za kupata faida zinazingatiwa na kuthamini utu wa
mtu, kuhakikisha mnawatendea haki wale mnaowapelekea bidhaa ili
wazinunue na kuzitumia kwa ajili ya kuendeleza uaminifu katika soko
ikiwa ni pamoja na kuwezesha upatikanaji wa ufanisi katika uchumi
wa soko, kujenga na kuimarisha mazingira sawa ya biashara katika
soko baina ya washindani, hayo yakifanikiwa bila shaka mtaweza
kushindana kwa vigezo vya ubora, bei, ubunifu na ufanisi.
Ndugu wanasemina, nimetaarifiwa kuwa kupitia semina hii pia
mtapata fursa ya kushauriana na kuelimishana kuhusu kazi za Tume
ya Ushindani (FCC) hususan katika masuala mbalimbali yanayohusu
udhibiti wa bidhaa bandia, ni vyema pia mkaitumia fursa hii vizuri kwa
kuwasilisha kero na changamoto mbalimbali mnazokabiliana nazo
katika shughuli zenu kwa watendaji wa FCC ili ziweze kupatiwa
majawabu yakinifu na kikamilifu.
Aidha, pamoja na juhudi hizi, ni vyema pia mkafanya jitihada ya
kutafuta masoko kupitia chama chenu (CTI) kwa kuzitumia Taasisi
mbalimbali za ndani na nje kwa msaada wa Mamlaka ya Usimamizi
na Maendeleo ya Biashara nchini, TANTRADE ili muweze kukuza
biashara zenu.
5

Naamini, ninyi ambao leo mmepata fursa ya semina hii, elimu
mtakayopata hapa mtakwenda kuwa mabalozi wazuri wa FCC katika
kuwaelimisha wananchi wengine ambao hawakupata fursa ya
kuhudhuria mafunzo haya.
Ndugu wanasemina, napenda kutumia fursa hii kwa niaba ya
Uongozi wa Serikali ya Mkoa wa Arusha kuwashukuru tena FCC kwa
kutuletea mafunzo haya hapa Arusha, nasi kama viongozi wa Serikali
na wananchi kwa ujumla tunawakaribisha tena wakati wowote
mtakaokuwa tayari kutuletea elimu za namna hii zenye maslahi
mapana kwa wananchi wetu na Taifa kwa ujumla hususan katika
masuala ya ushindani na ustawi wa uchumi.
Baada ya kusema hayo, nawatakia Semina njema na sasa natamka
kuwa Semina hii imefunguliwa rasmi.
Asanteni sana kwa kunisikiliza!
Speech by the Regional Commissioner of Arusha during the opening
of the Seminar on Competition Advocacy, Combat of Counterfeit
Goods, and Consumer Protection for Producers held at the Arusha
Regional Commissioner's Office on February 23, 2023.
Representative of the Director-General of the Fair Competition
Commission (FCC),
Chairman of the Confederation of Tanzania Industries (CTI) Arusha
Region,
6

Producers (CTI),
FCC Staff,
Trade Officer from the Arusha Regional Secretariat,
Journalists,
Invited Guests,
Ladies and Gentlemen.
First and foremost, I thank the Almighty God, full of mercy and grace,
for enabling us to meet in this event in good health. I also want to
warmly welcome the FCC, CTI, and all guests who have come from
outside the Arusha Region. Welcome!
The government of the Arusha Region is strong, and we assure you
of security, safety, and genuine cooperation in the development
activities of our nation throughout your stay here in Arusha.
I would like to use this opportunity to express my gratitude and
commendation to the sixth-phase government led by Her Excellency
Dr. Samia Suluhu Hassan, the President of the United Republic of
Tanzania, for the significant efforts it is making to bring development
to all Tanzanians, including enhancing productivity in the sectors of
investment, industry, and trade, including overall competition issues.
Furthermore, I commend the FCC for the effective implementation of
its duties according to the law, especially in matters of competition,
combat of counterfeit goods, and the overall protection of consumers.
7

These are crucial issues, and if we collaborate sincerely to oversee
them in accordance with the principles of the law, undoubtedly, this
sector of Industry, and Trade will thrive and contribute even more to
our country.
Seminar participants, today we have gathered here with the main
objective of receiving training on the roles of the Fair Competition
Commission, the Competition Act, combat of counterfeit goods, and
the responsibility of producers in protecting consumers. I thank the
FCC for recognizing the importance of bringing this seminar to our
Arusha Region. It is evident that you have made the right decision
considering the numerous production, tourism, and economic
activities taking place in our region.
Moreover, I congratulate the FCC for taking steps to conduct these
seminars with the aim of reaching a larger audience. However, there
is still extra work to be done to ensure that more seminars are held to
provide comprehensive education to our fellow Tanzanians, most of
whom are farmers, traders, and producers. This will enable them to
fully understand and position themselves in a competitive
environment according to the existing laws and regulations. The
Arusha Regional Government will collaborate with you, as mentioned
by the Director-General of the FCC.
Seminar participants, I am pleased to see your positive response,
especially since you are the producers, and you play a crucial role in
the future of economic growth, from household to national levels. To
prosper in your activities, it is imperative to adhere to the country's
8

regulations and principles of competition. This is why the FCC deems
it important to conduct these seminars for you. Therefore, you have a
role to carefully use this opportunity so that, after this training,
positive changes can be observed in your production activities and at
the national level.
The beneficiaries of today's seminar are the producers, so I urge
institutions, organizations, and other citizens engaged in competition
issues to cultivate a culture of seeking in-depth knowledge from the
FCC and other government departments, including the Small
Industries Development Organization (SIDO), Tanzania Bureau of
Standards (TBS), Business Registrations and Licensing Agency
(BRELA), and Weights and Measures Agency (WMA). I advise this
matter because these institutions, including the FCC, are crucial
bodies for the prosperity of business and market regulation in
Tanzania. If utilized properly, they will undoubtedly contribute
significantly to initiating, nurturing, and growing your businesses,
providing satisfactory results.
Therefore, all Directors of Local Government Authorities in the
Arusha Region should ensure that you identify groups or associations
involved in production and are served by the government through
your councils. Ensure that these groups receive training of this nature
to increase efficiency and value chain in their activities. This can be
achieved by building operational partnerships with these government
institutions, including the FCC, which, fundamentally, does an
excellent job in providing education to various development
stakeholders and the public at large. It also effectively controls
9

counterfeit goods in the country by conducting inspections in various
areas and entry points. Through cooperation with these institutions, I
believe the economic activities of our citizens, both in rural and urban
areas, will be safe and productive for the development of our people.
Therefore, all Directors of Local Government Authorities in the
Arusha Region should ensure that you have a good work plan to
coordinate the implementation of training for all groups benefiting
from government loans or funds that affect women, youth, and people
with disabilities. This training will undoubtedly empower them with
skills and expertise in production, sales, procurement, identification of
counterfeit goods, and understanding the principles of market
competition and the economy as a whole. Additionally, the
implementation of this work plan should consider involving institutions
such as the FCC in providing education.
Seminar participants, through this seminar, will receive various topics
that will build and provide essential foundations on business and the
economy, among other aspects that reflect progress in your daily
activities. Therefore, it is crucial that you pay careful attention to the
training opportunities presented here. After this training, positive
changes should be seen, including adhering to business ethics. This
is to ensure that the market remains competitive, products entering
the market meet consumer expectations, and profit-making
procedures are ethical and respect human dignity. Ensure that you
treat fairly those to whom you deliver products so that they can buy
and use them to maintain trust in the market and facilitate the
efficiency of the market economy, create and strengthen equal
10

business environments in the market among competitors. If
successful, you will undoubtedly compete based on quality, price,
innovation, and efficiency.
Seminar participants, I have been informed that through this seminar,
you will also have the opportunity to consult and educate each other
about the FCC functions, especially in various issues related to the
combat of counterfeit goods. It is essential to use this opportunity well
by presenting challenges and difficulties you face in your activities to
FCC officials so that they can be addressed comprehensively and
efficiently.
Furthermore, despite these efforts, it is also essential to make an
effort to seek markets through your association (CTI) by utilizing
various internal and external institutions with the assistance of the
Tanzania Trade Development Authority (TANTRADE) to grow your
businesses.
I believe those of you who have had the opportunity to attend this
seminar today will become good ambassadors of the FCC, educating
other citizens who did not have the chance to attend such training.
Seminar participants, I would like to use this opportunity, on behalf of
the Arusha Regional Government leadership, to thank the FCC once
again for this training. We, as government leaders and citizens in
general, welcome you anytime you are ready to bring us education
that is broadly beneficial to our people and the nation, particularly in
matters of competition and economic well-being.
11

After saying that, I wish
this
Thank
you a successful seminar, and I now declare
seminar officially open.
you very much for listening!
